10000.greenTrigger: Durable market-structure law plus workable final rules for custody, staking, tokenization, and on-chain finance.

10000.greenTrigger: Trillions in tokenized assets and stablecoins settle on Ethereum rails with clear ETH-denominated economic demand.
10000.redTrigger: L2 and app growth explodes while ETH fee burn, collateral demand, and settlement value remain weak.

10000.redTrigger: Ethereum becomes dominant infrastructure while fees, burn, collateral demand, and monetary premium accrue weakly to ETH.

5000.short: Structural fiscal pressure is separate from new cyclical data.
5000.summary: Large structural deficits and rising debt support the long-run case for scarce assets, even while positive real yields delay the cleanest expression of that trade.
5000.evidence: Prior fiscal figures remain Reuters-attributed without independent Treasury retrieval; dated CBO projections remain forecasts. China's new real-activity release and technology-transfer policy do not establish debt monetization or an ETH reserve allocation. No structural score change is justified.

5000.greenTrigger: Debt-service pressure rises while real yields and the dollar fall, and ETH participates in flows toward scarce assets.
5000.redTrigger: Fiscal consolidation gains credibility, real yields stay structurally high, or the debasement bid flows almost entirely to BTC and gold.

10000.short: ETH must still earn a persistent monetary/collateral premium.
10000.summary: Fiscal stress can expand demand for scarce assets, but the $10K thesis needs ETH itself to become a durable monetary, collateral, and productive-capital asset.
10000.evidence: Neither fiscal anxiety nor the new China growth data proves multi-year reserve allocation to ETH. Preserve the earlier fiscal-source qualification and the independent requirement for durable staking, collateral and monetary demand; retain yellow.
10000.why: A $1.2T ETH valuation becomes more credible if allocators treat ETH as productive reserve collateral, not merely as a high-beta technology asset.
10000.greenTrigger: Multi-year allocation to ETH as a reserve, collateral, and staking asset grows while real yields fall and fiscal dominance becomes more visible.
10000.redTrigger: BTC, gold, or stablecoin yields absorb the debasement trade while ETH remains valued mainly on application activity.

changes.title: ETF outflows and the yield shock broke the recent base
changes.summary: Seven consecutive U.S. spot ETH ETF sessions removed about $568.8M while ETH fell roughly 5.2% from the October 5 snapshot to about $2.56K. With the 10-year Treasury yield near 5.34%, Brent around $104.75, and the dollar close to an 18-month high, $5K institutional demand moved from green to yellow and $5K market structure moved from yellow to red. The $5K estimate fell four points and the $10K estimate fell three points; the structural debasement lens stayed separate and the $10K value-capture hurdle remained red.

changes.title: SEC staking guidance moved U.S. regulation from red to yellow
changes.summary: SEC Corporation Finance staff FAQs clarified that qualifying staking-receipt tokens can be digital tools or digital commodities and that routine work on functional crypto networks generally is not an essential managerial effort under Howey. The regulatory catalyst improved for both targets, while probabilities stayed at 62% and 30% because the guidance is nonbinding, broader legislation remains stalled, macro conditions are restrictive, and the $10K value-capture hurdle remains unresolved.

changes.title: Treasury yield shock reversed part of the breakout gain
changes.summary: The U.S. 10-year yield reached 5.106%, ETH fell 4%, and Ethereum bridge flows turned negative, reducing both target probabilities by one point. The structural debasement thesis remained unchanged because no QE or monetization signal appeared.
